title: EntropyStop: Unsupervised Deep Outlier Detection with Loss Entropy

problem.claim: Deep unsupervised outlier detection aims to learn the distribution of normal data from training data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches face either the need for manually cleaned datasets or robustness and training-time challenges when using contaminated unlabeled data and ensembles.

contributions.claim: The paper presents EntropyStop, an unsupervised deep outlier detection method using loss entropy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Unsupervised outlier detection is an important data mining task with broad interest in deep learning.
Most deep unsupervised models rely on clean datasets, creating substantial data-cleaning effort for real-world data.
Training and detecting directly on contaminated unlabeled datasets creates a need for robust methods.
Ensembles improve robustness against contaminated training sets but substantially increase training time.

source_observation.claim: Contaminated unlabeled training data creates robustness challenges, while ensemble methods increase training time.

interpretation.claim: Robustness improvements may involve a computational trade-off.

application.claim: When designing unsupervised detection systems for imperfect data, evaluate both contamination robustness and training cost.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this trade-off applies beyond the described outlier-detection setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe how loss entropy is used.
No experimental datasets, baselines, metrics, results, or numerical findings are supplied.
The abstract does not establish the method's robustness or training-time performance.
